blocks.explanation:
Two angles given by one ratio each and their quadrants.
We must find \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\).
Plan: complete the ratios of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) with the correct signs, then use the formula.
steps:
Given: \(\sin\alpha = -\frac{8}{17}\) (\(\alpha\) in quadrant IV), \(\cos\beta = -\frac{4}{5}\) (\(\beta\) in quadrant III).
To find: \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\).
Method: \[\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta\]
First find \(\cos\alpha\) and \(\sin\beta\), using the quadrants for the signs.

Find the missing ratios
\[\cos\alpha = +\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{64}{289}} = \dfrac{15}{17}\]
\[\sin\beta = -\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{16}{25}} = -\dfrac{3}{5}\]
Why: In quadrant IV cosine is positive; in quadrant III sine is negative.

Substitute
\[= \left(-\dfrac{8}{17}\right)\left(-\dfrac{4}{5}\right) + \dfrac{15}{17}\left(-\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{32}{85} - \dfrac{45}{85} = -\dfrac{13}{85}\]
Why: Negative times negative is positive; positive times negative is negative.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(-\frac{56}{65}\) for part (i). This does not fit the printed data: with \(\sin\alpha = -\frac{8}{17}\), \(\cos\alpha = \frac{15}{17}\), \(\sin\beta = -\frac{3}{5}\), \(\cos\beta = -\frac{4}{5}\) every answer has denominator 85, not 65. The correct value is \(-\dfrac{13}{85}\).

blocks.explanation:
Two angles given by one ratio each and their quadrants.
We must find \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\).
Plan: complete the ratios of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) with the correct signs, then use the formula.
steps:
Given: \(\sin\alpha = -\frac{8}{17}\) (\(\alpha\) in quadrant IV), \(\cos\beta = -\frac{4}{5}\) (\(\beta\) in quadrant III).
To find: \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\).
Method: \[\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
First find \(\cos\alpha\) and \(\sin\beta\), using the quadrants for the signs.

Find the missing ratios
\[\cos\alpha = +\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{64}{289}} = \dfrac{15}{17}\]
\[\sin\beta = -\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{16}{25}} = -\dfrac{3}{5}\]
Why: In quadrant IV cosine is positive; in quadrant III sine is negative.

Substitute
\[= \dfrac{15}{17}\left(-\dfrac{4}{5}\right) - \left(-\dfrac{8}{17}\right)\left(-\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\]
\[= -\dfrac{60}{85} - \dfrac{24}{85} = -\dfrac{84}{85}\]
Why: The second product is \(+\frac{24}{85}\), and it is subtracted.

Check
\[13^2 + 84^2 = 85^2\]
Why: With part (i), \(\sin^2(\alpha + \beta) + \cos^2(\alpha + \beta) = 1\) \(\checkmark\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(-\frac{33}{65}\) for part (ii). This does not fit the printed data: with \(\sin\alpha = -\frac{8}{17}\), \(\cos\alpha = \frac{15}{17}\), \(\sin\beta = -\frac{3}{5}\), \(\cos\beta = -\frac{4}{5}\) every answer has denominator 85, not 65. The correct value is \(-\dfrac{84}{85}\).

blocks.explanation:
Two angles given by one ratio each and their quadrants.
We must find \(\tan(\alpha + \beta)\).
Plan: complete the ratios of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) with the correct signs, then use the formula.
steps:
Given: \(\sin\alpha = -\frac{8}{17}\) (\(\alpha\) in quadrant IV), \(\cos\beta = -\frac{4}{5}\) (\(\beta\) in quadrant III).
To find: \(\tan(\alpha + \beta)\).
Method: \[\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{\sin(\alpha + \beta)}{\cos(\alpha + \beta)}\]
using the sine and cosine of \(\alpha + \beta\) (parts (i) and (ii)).
First find \(\cos\alpha\) and \(\sin\beta\), using the quadrants for the signs.

Find the missing ratios
\[\cos\alpha = +\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{64}{289}} = \dfrac{15}{17}\]
\[\sin\beta = -\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{16}{25}} = -\dfrac{3}{5}\]
Why: In quadrant IV cosine is positive; in quadrant III sine is negative.

Sine and cosine of \(\alpha + \beta\)
\[\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{32}{85} - \dfrac{45}{85} = -\dfrac{13}{85}\]
\[\cos(\alpha + \beta) = -\dfrac{60}{85} - \dfrac{24}{85} = -\dfrac{84}{85}\]
Why: Same working as parts (i) and (ii).
@@Divide
\[\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{-13/85}{-84/85} = \dfrac{13}{84}\]
Why: The 85s cancel; negative over negative is positive.

Check
\[\tan\alpha = -\dfrac{8}{15},\ \tan\beta = \dfrac{3}{4}\]
\[\dfrac{-\frac{8}{15} + \frac{3}{4}}{1 + \frac{8}{15}\cdot\frac{3}{4}} \]
\[= \dfrac{13/60}{84/60} = \dfrac{13}{84} \;\checkmark\]
Why: The tangent formula gives the same value.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(\frac{56}{33}\) for part (iii). This does not fit the printed data: with \(\sin\alpha = -\frac{8}{17}\), \(\cos\alpha = \frac{15}{17}\), \(\sin\beta = -\frac{3}{5}\), \(\cos\beta = -\frac{4}{5}\) every answer has denominator 85, not 65. The correct value is \(\dfrac{13}{84}\).

blocks.explanation:
Two angles given by one ratio each and their quadrants.
We must find \(\sin(\alpha - \beta)\).
Plan: complete the ratios of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) with the correct signs, then use the formula.
steps:
Given: \(\sin\alpha = -\frac{8}{17}\) (\(\alpha\) in quadrant IV), \(\cos\beta = -\frac{4}{5}\) (\(\beta\) in quadrant III).
To find: \(\sin(\alpha - \beta)\).
Method: \[\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta - \cos\alpha\sin\beta\]
First find \(\cos\alpha\) and \(\sin\beta\), using the quadrants for the signs.

Find the missing ratios
\[\cos\alpha = +\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{64}{289}} = \dfrac{15}{17}\]
\[\sin\beta = -\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{16}{25}} = -\dfrac{3}{5}\]
Why: In quadrant IV cosine is positive; in quadrant III sine is negative.

Substitute
\[= \left(-\dfrac{8}{17}\right)\left(-\dfrac{4}{5}\right) - \dfrac{15}{17}\left(-\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{32}{85} + \dfrac{45}{85} = \dfrac{77}{85}\]
Why: Minus a negative product becomes plus.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(\frac{16}{65}\) for part (iv). This does not fit the printed data: with \(\sin\alpha = -\frac{8}{17}\), \(\cos\alpha = \frac{15}{17}\), \(\sin\beta = -\frac{3}{5}\), \(\cos\beta = -\frac{4}{5}\) every answer has denominator 85, not 65. The correct value is \(\dfrac{77}{85}\).

blocks.explanation:
Two angles given by one ratio each and their quadrants.
We must find \(\cos(\alpha - \beta)\).
Plan: complete the ratios of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) with the correct signs, then use the formula.
steps:
Given: \(\sin\alpha = -\frac{8}{17}\) (\(\alpha\) in quadrant IV), \(\cos\beta = -\frac{4}{5}\) (\(\beta\) in quadrant III).
To find: \(\cos(\alpha - \beta)\).
Method: \[\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
First find \(\cos\alpha\) and \(\sin\beta\), using the quadrants for the signs.

Find the missing ratios
\[\cos\alpha = +\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{64}{289}} = \dfrac{15}{17}\]
\[\sin\beta = -\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{16}{25}} = -\dfrac{3}{5}\]
Why: In quadrant IV cosine is positive; in quadrant III sine is negative.

Substitute
\[= \dfrac{15}{17}\left(-\dfrac{4}{5}\right) + \left(-\dfrac{8}{17}\right)\left(-\dfrac{3}{5}\right)\]
\[= -\dfrac{60}{85} + \dfrac{24}{85} = -\dfrac{36}{85}\]
Why: For cosine of a difference the products are added.

Check
\[77^2 + 36^2 = 85^2\]
Why: With part (iv), \(\sin^2 + \cos^2 = 1\) \(\checkmark\).

blocks.text: The answer key prints \(\frac{63}{65}\) for part (v). This does not fit the printed data: with \(\sin\alpha = -\frac{8}{17}\), \(\cos\alpha = \frac{15}{17}\), \(\sin\beta = -\frac{3}{5}\), \(\cos\beta = -\frac{4}{5}\) every answer has denominator 85, not 65. The correct value is \(-\dfrac{36}{85}\).

blocks.explanation:
Two angles given by one ratio each and their quadrants.
We must find \(\tan(\alpha - \beta)\).
Plan: complete the ratios of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) with the correct signs, then use the formula.
steps:
Given: \(\sin\alpha = -\frac{8}{17}\) (\(\alpha\) in quadrant IV), \(\cos\beta = -\frac{4}{5}\) (\(\beta\) in quadrant III).
To find: \(\tan(\alpha - \beta)\).
Method: \[\tan(\alpha - \beta) = \dfrac{\sin(\alpha - \beta)}{\cos(\alpha - \beta)}\]
using parts (iv) and (v).
First find \(\cos\alpha\) and \(\sin\beta\), using the quadrants for the signs.

Find the missing ratios
\[\cos\alpha = +\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{64}{289}} = \dfrac{15}{17}\]
\[\sin\beta = -\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{16}{25}} = -\dfrac{3}{5}\]
Why: In quadrant IV cosine is positive; in quadrant III sine is negative.

Sine and cosine of \(\alpha - \beta\)
\[\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \dfrac{32}{85} + \dfrac{45}{85} = \dfrac{77}{85}\]
\[\cos(\alpha - \beta) = -\dfrac{60}{85} + \dfrac{24}{85} = -\dfrac{36}{85}\]
Why: Same working as parts (iv) and (v).
@@Divide
\[\tan(\alpha - \beta) = \dfrac{77/85}{-36/85} = -\dfrac{77}{36}\]
Why: The 85s cancel; positive over negative is negative.

Check
\[\dfrac{-\frac{8}{15} - \frac{3}{4}}{1 - \frac{8}{15}\cdot\frac{3}{4}} \]
\[= \dfrac{-77/60}{36/60} = -\dfrac{77}{36} \;\checkmark\]
Why: The tangent difference formula gives the same value.

This does not fit the printed data: with \(\sin\alpha = -\frac{8}{17}\), \(\cos\alpha = \frac{15}{17}\), \(\sin\beta = -\frac{3}{5}\), \(\cos\beta = -\frac{4}{5}\) every answer has denominator 85, not 65. The correct value is \(-\dfrac{77}{36}\).

blocks.prompt: 9 (vii) [printed without a label] If \(\sin\alpha = -\dfrac{8}{17}\) and \(\cos\beta = -\dfrac{4}{5}\) where \(\dfrac{3\pi}{2} < \alpha < 2\pi\) and \(\pi < \beta < \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\). In which quadrants do the terminal sides of the angles of measures \((\alpha + \beta)\) and \((\alpha - \beta)\) lie?
blocks.explanation:
The quadrant of an angle is decided by the signs of its sine and cosine.
We have \(\sin\) and \(\cos\) of \(\alpha + \beta\) and \(\alpha - \beta\) from parts (i), (ii), (iv), (v).
Plan: read the signs and match them with the quadrant chart.
steps:
Given: \(\sin(\alpha + \beta) = -\frac{13}{85}\), \(\cos(\alpha + \beta) = -\frac{84}{85}\), \(\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \frac{77}{85}\), \(\cos(\alpha - \beta) = -\frac{36}{85}\).
To find: the quadrants of \(\alpha + \beta\) and \(\alpha - \beta\).
Method: sine is positive in I and II; cosine is positive in I and IV.

Quadrant of \(\alpha + \beta\)
\[\sin(\alpha + \beta) < 0,\quad \cos(\alpha + \beta) < 0\]
\[\Rightarrow \text{quadrant III}\]
Why: Negative sine means III or IV; negative cosine means II or III; the common one is III.

Quadrant of \(\alpha - \beta\)
\[\sin(\alpha - \beta) > 0,\quad \cos(\alpha - \beta) < 0\]
\[\Rightarrow \text{quadrant II}\]
Why: Positive sine means I or II; negative cosine means II or III; the common one is II.

Check with the angle sizes
\[270^{\circ} < \alpha < 360^{\circ},\quad 180^{\circ} < \beta < 270^{\circ}\]
\[\alpha \approx 331.9^{\circ},\ \beta \approx 216.9^{\circ}\]
\[\alpha + \beta \approx 548.8^{\circ} \equiv 188.8^{\circ}\ (\text{III})\]
\[\alpha - \beta \approx 115.1^{\circ}\ (\text{II}) \;\checkmark\]
Why: Subtracting \(360^{\circ}\) does not change the terminal side.
blocks.final_answer: \(\alpha + \beta\) lies in quadrant III and \(\alpha - \beta\) lies in quadrant II.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key says the terminal arms of \(\alpha + \beta\) and \(\alpha - \beta\) are in quadrants III and I. With the printed data \(\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \frac{77}{85} > 0\) and \(\cos(\alpha - \beta) = -\frac{36}{85} < 0\), so \(\alpha - \beta\) is in quadrant II, not I. \(\alpha + \beta\) is in quadrant III.
